title: Socio-Culturally Aware Evaluation Framework for LLM-Based Content Moderation
findings: In the hate speech generation task (HATE-GEN), religious beliefs were a key factor. The study found that Protestant and Taoist personas tended to oppose hate speech, while Baptist personas were more prone to generating hateful content. Atheist and Catholic personas maintained a balance, Muslim and Hindu personas showed moderate tendencies, and Jewish personas leaned toward opposing hate speech.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures how Large Language Models generate hateful content and exhibit biases when prompted with personas having specific religious attributes. It analyzes how different religious identities influence the tone and content of generated text, particularly in the context of hate speech.
